findings.reason: the plan presents this as a mechanism "the registry already offers"; it does not, so a node following it would search for a definition field that is never there and stall on the first sentence.
findings.text: §5 tells the worker to place each sentence on "the definition of the component, zone or population token that only those names carry", but no such definition exists: `_vocabulary_definitions()` (imas_standard_names/grammar/vocab_loaders.py:715-724) returns definitions only for locus, physical_base and geometry_carrier tokens, and a `concepts.yml` entry (which must carry exactly one canonical equation and is keyed by an operator/locus/coordinate/base token, §2 and the file's own header) cannot be keyed by `cold`, `thermal`, `upper` or `total` — so a population, zone or aggregation token has nowhere to carry the sentence, and `select_conventions` returns nothing at all for `cold_neutral_temperature` and `total_electron_density`

findings.reason: the control the done-when advertises ("fails again with a sentence moved to the shared template") is not uniform; the density sentence needs a density sibling outside the trio, exactly as the neutral sentence has electron/ion temperature, or the test proves nothing for that sentence.
findings.text: the electron-density sentence cannot be rendered on exactly {total_electron_density, thermal_electron_density, fast_electron_density} by any template: `total_electron_density` fills the `aggregation` segment while `thermal`/`fast` fill `population` (two different segment kinds), and `select_conventions` matches templates by segment kind through a subset test (`templates.py`/`grammar/terms.py:305`, `set(entry.segments) <= segments`), so any template that reaches all three also reaches every other density name; and because the done-when adds a sibling outside the family ("at least electron_temperature and ion_temperature") only beside the neutral pair, its "on no other name" half can never fail for the electron-density sentence, so a sentence dropped onto the shared `density`/`[subject]` template passes both halves

findings.reason: the two triangularity rulings share a sentence and one base family, so the plan's three-sentence list still covers every name that carries a sentence; the count is descriptive, not a coverage contract.
findings.text: §5 states "Three of those rulings carry a `template_sentence`", but the cited JSON carries four rulings with a non-null `template_sentence` (overlap-296b9d67a4a5, overlap-370569d04611, overlap-7f2595983ef6, overlap-ff9acc486ea4), the two triangularity rulings sharing one sentence
